chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام) when Mihzam entered upon him and said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, inform me about this matter that we are awaiting—when will it be?” He said: “O Mihzam, the time-setters have lied, the hasty ones are ruined, and the submitting ones are saved.”

key_terms.الْمُسَلِّمُونَ: those who submit and surrender to the divine matter
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعْجِلُونَ: those who are impatient and seek to hasten the matter
key_terms.الْوَقَّاتُونَ: those who set specific times for the event
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the awaited matter, referring here to the divinely ordained affair being anticipated

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) say about setting a time for the reappearance?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that assigning a fixed time to the awaited matter is false and condemned. It warns against impatience and teaches that safety lies in submission, restraint, and faithful acceptance regarding the affair of the Imam's reappearance.
